prompt:
PostgreSQL 16. This report query went from 2s to 9 minutes and I can't see why — the indexes are there and autovacuum/autoanalyze ran an hour ago. Should I add a composite index?

SELECT c.id, c.name, SUM(o.total)
FROM customers c
JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
WHERE c.city = 'Hanoi' AND c.country = 'VN'
GROUP BY c.id, c.name;

customers: 9M rows, indexes customers_city_idx (city), customers_country_idx (country). orders: 140M rows, index orders_customer_id_idx (customer_id).
Every customer in Hanoi is in VN. ~480k customers are in Hanoi; ~2.1M are in VN.

EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) excerpt:
HashAggregate (actual time=541203..541880 rows=479812)
  -> Nested Loop (cost=1.13..2051.40 rows=112 width=40) (actual time=0.09..532011 rows=7398120 loops=1)
       -> Bitmap Heap Scan on customers c (cost=..  rows=112 ...) (actual rows=479812 loops=1)
             Recheck Cond: ((city = 'Hanoi') AND (country = 'VN'))
             -> BitmapAnd
                  -> Bitmap Index Scan on customers_city_idx (rows=480100) (actual rows=479812)
                  -> Bitmap Index Scan on customers_country_idx (rows=2100500) (actual rows=2103377)
       -> Index Scan using orders_customer_id_idx on orders o (cost=0.57..18.20 rows=15) (actual rows=15 loops=479812)
            Buffers: shared hit=1203411 read=6211040
assertions: The response identifies the estimate of 112 rows vs 479,812 actual on customers as the root cause of the slow nested loop
The response explains that the planner multiplies the selectivities of city and country as if independent, although Hanoi implies VN
The response recommends CREATE STATISTICS (dependencies and/or mcv) ON city, country FROM customers followed by ANALYZE
The response says a composite index is not the main fix (at most secondary), since the misestimate is the problem
The response explains that with a correct estimate the planner would choose a different join strategy for orders (e.g. hash join / scan of orders) instead of 480k index lookups
The response notes that autoanalyze already ran, so a plain ANALYZE / stale statistics is not the explanation
The response gives a verification step: re-run EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) and check that the customers estimate is close to ~480k
Each reported issue carries an explicit severity label (e.g. High / Medium / Low, or Critical / Major / Minor); ordering alone does not count
